item.content:encoded:
"…requisite ball of twine…"
While an awesome classical detail, wouldn't it be better to use something less fragile? Something that couldn't easily snap while rubbing on the door edges or tugging too hard as an explorer walks along?
High-tensile fishing line would be suitable, off the top of my head.

In any case, such a requirement should be included in the containment procedures. Something like: All entrants are required to follow standard path-marking protocols. See addendum 167-Alpha.
I enjoyed it, put it that way.

item.content:encoded:
The reclassification to Safe means that the third Addendum does not make sense without a denial of the proposal. The redaction in containment procedures is bothersome, and could be re-written to simply remove the offending information without losing anything. The cross-testing with SCP-184 highlights the age of the article without really adding that much of relevance to it (but would make an interesting Tale). Finding SCPs inside of the SCP is another anachronism that has fallen out of favor. Then as Decibelles points out, the whole "keter duty" is old school.

Ultimately without a re-write I have to give this one a -1.

item.content:encoded:
It seems like it would be straight-forward enough to make the maze easier to escape by, say, painting an 'OUT' sign on each door after you pass through it. Since the topology of the maze appears to be a binary tree with no intersection, this should ensure people always travel to the 'root' of the tree, i.e., the exit. At the very least, this implies that someone who follows an 'out' door should always arrive closer to the exit than they would have otherwise.

That should prevent incidents like Dr. XXXXX's disappearance, or at least make them less likely.

If this DOESN'T work, that too will be educational as to the nature of the SCP.
